_readme: Roster and rules for the daily comment scan. Consumed by the `comment-scan` skill, which writes campaign/commentQueue via scripts/push-comment-queue.mjs. Rules here were derived by hand on 2026-08-18 and are recorded in grading-lessons.md; do not loosen them to manufacture work.
why: A reshare puts someone else's post in front of our ~0 followers. A comment puts us in front of the people already engaging with a post that is working. Out-of-network reach is earned by borrowing an audience, not by posting harder.
howToScan: Walk each target's activity page — https://www.linkedin.com/in/<slug>/recent-activity/all/ — and pull permalinks from the DOM. Hashtag SEARCH results carry no urn:li:activity, so nothing found there can be queued; use the feeds only to discover new names for this roster. Learned 2026-08-25. A target activity page mixes their own posts with their reshares — check for a "reposted this" line and take the byline UNDERNEATH it as the author.

timing.why: Dave is rarely at his desk before 09:30 (stated 2026-08-26), so the old 07:15 slot was a time nobody was there for. A comment's visibility still tracks the HOST post's audience — US-heavy, most active mid-morning Eastern — and 09:30 CT is 10:30 ET, which is inside that window. This is the opposite of our own posts at 19:20 CT, a different mechanic.
timing.scanBy: 05:36 CT, unattended — the queue only has to be ready before Dave is.

selection.targetShape: high reactions, LOW comments — a big audience looking and almost nobody talking
hardRules: NEVER queue a RESHARE. Open the post page and read who actually wrote it — a reshare shows the resharer at the top and the real author underneath. On 2026-08-26 a post was queued under Markus Kopko that Hiromi Nakatani wrote; the drafted comment referenced a piece of Markus own writing she had never published. Commenting on a reshare also puts us in a stranger room under a roster name, which is not the audience we chose.
The host post must still be LIVE. A two-week-old post with 200 reactions is a dead room; all-time counts mean nothing.
Skip any post already past maxHostComments — a comment is buried on arrival.

Video posts are NEVER a dead end (2026-08-31). Try the FRAME first: Andrew Ramdayal’s practice-question clips print the whole stem and all four options on screen — navigate to the permalink, wait ~5s, and zoom a screenshot of the video region. Do not click the middle of the video to play it; that hits a link and navigates away. If there is nothing to read, TRANSCRIBE it: `node scripts/transcribe-post-video.mjs <post-url>` runs yt-dlp + ffmpeg + faster-whisper entirely on this machine — no API key, no cost, no cookies — and caches to site/data/video-transcripts/. Put the result on the item as `transcript` and the Comments page renders it. `manual` is now only for genuine failures (download fails, no speech, unintelligible) and you must say which. This was built because a Ramdayal talking-head clip sat in `manual` for three days at 28-31 reactions and ZERO comments, one day from ageing out, purely because nobody could hear it. Also read the EXISTING comments before drafting: on Question 91 all nine said only "A" with no reasoning, which is what made a comment explaining the distractor worth writing.
If we cannot say something true that a PMP or Security+ candidate would not already know, SKIP. No 'great post' filler, ever.

On a WIN post (someone passed), congratulate first and aim any teaching at people who will copy them — never correct the person celebrating. Dave flagged the first draft of one of these as aggressive and he was right.
Never mention CipherExam, a trial, or a link in a comment. The payoff is profile views and follows, not clicks.
Skip recruiter and job-ad posts even when the room is huge. A 440-reaction job listing has no opening for anything true about exam reasoning.
selection.lowReachException: A small room (under ~10 reactions) is still worth a comment when the host is a genuine peer and comment count is zero — yours is the only one they read. Mark those as a relationship play, not reach.

measurement.metric: profile viewers and followers, read off Dave's LinkedIn sidebar
measurement.why: The payoff from commenting is people who read it and came to look — not likes on the comment itself. Without a before-number there is nothing to compare against.

rosterHealth: Every slug below was read out of a real LinkedIn page on 2026-08-25 — none are guessed. `confidence` says how much we actually know: `proven` means we have seen the person post on-topic with measured engagement; `likely` means the profile is real and on-topic but reach is unmeasured; `unproven` means the name surfaced on a cert hashtag and nothing more. Each scan should record what it observes and DROP unproven names that never post with reach. A roster full of silent accounts wastes the scan.

targets.name: Andrew Ramdayal
targets.audience: PMP candidates — the largest on the platform
targets.note: 29 reactions / 1 comment at 23h on 2026-08-25 — the best room found that day. Every post is VIDEO, so never auto-draft: send to `manual` for Dave to watch and answer live. Scanned 2026-08-30: three live video rooms — Practice Question 91 at 70r/9c (20h), Question 90 at 78r/14c (1.9d), and a study-advice clip at 28r/ZERO comments (1.7d). Still the biggest rooms available to us anywhere, and still all video. Same three sent to manual as on 08-29, which means the previous batch went unanswered. BREAKTHROUGH 2026-08-30: his practice-question videos are READABLE without audio — the full stem and all four options are burned into the frame as text, so they can be screenshotted and answered. Question 91 (70r/9c) and Question 90 (78r/14c) were both drafted this way instead of going to manual. His non-question clips ("Don’t do this when studying") are talking head only, no on-screen text, no caption track, and still need Dave. This roughly doubles what the scan can queue, because his rooms are by far the largest we can reach. Scanned 2026-08-31: Question 91 grew to 91r/12c (1.9d) and Question 90 to 86r/16c (2.9d) — both still under the cap and both QUEUED again, because yesterday's batch went unposted. The new one, Question 92, took 95 reactions and TWENTY-TWO comments in 0.9 days and is the FIRST question post of his to blow the 20-comment cap. Revise the timing rule accordingly: his question videos are the biggest rooms we can reach, but they only qualify inside roughly the first 24 hours now, and Question 90 shows the count still creeping (14 to 16 overnight) days later. Queue him same-day or not at all. AUDIO SOLVED 2026-08-31: his talking-head clips can now be transcribed locally (scripts/transcribe-post-video.mjs). The “Don’t do this when studying” clip — stuck in `manual` since 08-29 — was transcribed and drafted at 31 reactions / ZERO comments. His argument in it is OUR thesis: do not memorise the ITTOs, understand them. `videoOnly` no longer means unanswerable for any target. Scanned 2026-09-01: Question 93 (vendor factory acceptance test, answer D) at 92r/11c in 20.7h — QUEUED, and the eleven comments are the Question 91 pattern again, nine bare letter Ds with one short assess-first note, so the distractor teardown is effectively the first substantive reply. Question 92 confirmed the new timing rule hard: it went from 95r/22c to 126r/24c and is now well past the cap, so his question videos really are a same-day-or-never target. Two talking-head clips also landed, "Hardest topic on the PMP" at 23r/ZERO comments (17.7h, transcribed, QUEUED — his argument is that the project management plan is an artifact with nearly 20 components you should build rather than read about, which is our thesis in his words) and "Tips for the PMP and CAPM" at 17r/0c, which was left unqueued ONLY to avoid three comments on one profile in one morning on top of the three Dave posted yesterday. Standing cap from here: at most two Ramdayal items per run, biggest room first. His CISSP course promo at 9r/1c is a sales post with no exam-reasoning opening — skip that shape. Scanned 2026-09-02: five posts, all inside 22 hours. QUEUED TWO, which is the standing cap. Practice Question 94 (delivery team, requirements enter the sprint unclear and stay unclear; answer B, product owner reviews backlog refinement) at 53r/7c in 20.6h — and all seven comments are the bare letter B with no reasoning, the Question 91 pattern for the third time. The frame was readable again, no transcription needed. Second pick is "Two different mindsets for the PMP" at 24r/ZERO comments in 21.6h, a talking-head clip transcribed locally: he separates the project manager mindset (accountability, proactive) from the PMP exam mindset (analyze before solving, do not fire people). That separation IS our thesis, stated by the biggest instructor on the platform, which makes it the easiest build-next-to-him comment on the roster. Left off for the cap: a case-study video series launch, "How to always pick the right answer choice on the PMP" at 11r/0c, and a live Q&A promo. Also dropped the unposted 08-31 item (project management plan clip, now 41.5h at 23r) because the two newer rooms are bigger and the cap is two. Worth noting for the cap rule: his non-question clips reliably sit at ZERO comments for a full day, so they are not the scarce resource his question videos are — the question videos are the ones that must be same-day.

targets.name: Markus Kopko
targets.note: GAVE US OUR ONLY TESTIMONIAL and sits on the PMI AI Standards Core Team. Build next to him, never against him — never name him as a competitor, never counter his content. His three-state self-scoring post (2026-08-20) is the structure we want to borrow, rewritten. Scanned 2026-08-29: activity page is almost all reshares; his one original (1r/1c at 1h) was a bus-factor note ending in a link to his own PM Career OS community. No exam-reasoning opening. Scanned 2026-08-30: two originals, the same PgMP-pass-in-three-numbers post in English (4r/1c) and German (2r/1c), both under the floor. Everything else on the page is a reshare of PMI AI-standard content. BREAKTHROUGH 2026-08-31 — QUEUED for the first time. He posted our thesis nearly verbatim: "Most candidates who fail the PMP never had a knowledge problem. They had a selection problem, and they found out on exam day." Reading produces recognition; the exam drops you into a delivery week with four defensible options and ninety seconds. He also names the 9 July 2026 case-study sets, where a misread at the top of a linked set travels through every question below it. 6r/4c at one hour, and TWO of those four comments are his own reveal links and a third is a one-line paraphrase, so a substantive reply is effectively the first real comment. IMPORTANT correction to this entry: he links a PMP exam simulator of his own (pmp-sim.pm-career-os.de) and is launching a free 30-day one-scenario-a-day series, so he is a DIRECT format competitor, not just a PMI-adjacent peer. The relationship rule is unchanged and now matters more — build next to him, never against him, never name a tool. Scanned 2026-09-01: no new original post since the selection-problem post Dave commented on. His entire page today is reshares, including two reshares of that same post and one of Marco Botel and one of Joshua Barnes. The self-reshare pattern is worth knowing — it makes his activity page look busy when he has written nothing new, so always check the reposted-this line before counting a post as fresh. Scanned 2026-09-02: every item on his page is a reshare — PMI's WBS blog, a Project Management Life magazine announcement, a Joshua Barnes open-to-work appeal, and TWO self-reshares of his own posts including the selection-problem one Dave already commented on. Second consecutive day of nothing original. The self-reshare pattern is now confirmed twice: his activity page looks busy while he has written nothing new, so always check the reposted-this line before counting a post as fresh.
